How Far Ahead Should You Book a Luxury Egypt Trip?

Nine to twelve months for Christmas, six to nine for Easter, weeks for summer: how far ahead to book a private Egypt journey, and what sells out first

07 November 2026 · 13 minute read

By Islam Hussein, Sillage Égypte journey designer. Last updated: November 2026.

The quick answer

Count back from your dates: nine to twelve months for Christmas, New Year and event dates; six to nine for Easter; four to six for high winter; three to six for the October to November and March to April shoulders; six to ten weeks in summer. A 25% non-refundable deposit secures the booking, and the balance is due 60 days before arrival. What runs out first is never the sites. It is the small boats and the Nile-view suites.

Lead time by season

Season When it falls How far ahead to book What goes first

Easter Two Easters: 28 March and 2 May in 2027 6 to 9 months Boats and suites around each holiday week

Lead times are the experience of our journey designers with private travel (as of November 2026). They are not hard rules, and the reasons behind each row follow below.

Almost every enquiry we receive opens with a calendar question rather than an Egypt question: we are thinking of December, or perhaps Easter, so when do we actually need to book? The honest answer is that it depends almost entirely on the week you choose. Egypt's lead times are set not by seats on aircraft but by small, date-bound inventory (small boats, suites above the Nile, permissions tied to a single morning), and that inventory disappears to a seasonal rhythm. This post sets the rhythm out: how far ahead each season really needs, what sells out first, how to book around events from the Abu Simbel Sun Festival to the 2027 eclipse, and, just as useful, what can comfortably wait. Sillage Égypte (sillage-egypte.com) is a private Egypt journey designer, and what follows is how far ahead our designers ask travellers to come to us, season by season.

The short answer: how far ahead to book

Most private Egypt journeys are best booked between three months and a year ahead, and the span is wide because Egypt's seasons are unequal. Book nine to twelve months out for the festive fortnight and for event dates; six to nine for Easter; four to six for high winter; three to six for the shoulders; six to ten weeks in summer. Inside those windows you choose freely; beyond them you choose from what remains.

The reason is scarcity, not bureaucracy. A dahabiya, a shallow-draught traditional Nile sailing boat with typically 8 to 12 cabins, air-conditioned and en suite, and a full crew, can be chartered privately by one party, so when one party takes New Year's Eve on the river, that boat is gone for everyone else. Suites at the Nile-side hotels sell before standard rooms. Dated permissions, such as two hours with the Giza plateau reserved for your party, are never held on request and never promised.

Because every Sillage journey is private throughout (your own car, your own certified Egyptologist from the first day to the last and, on the dahabiya journeys, your own boat), your booking claims whole things rather than places on them, which is why we ask for dates earlier than a scheduled tour would need them. A signature journey such as The Complete Egypt, 13 days and 12 nights with five nights on a private dahabiya between Esna and Aswan, is from €7,500 per person (for two or more travellers, in luxury hotels, as listed in November 2026), and the festive fortnight has a journey of its own, Christmas & New Year on the Nile, 14 days and 13 nights from €9,999. Each is only a starting point; the calendar, like the hotels, is tailored entirely. Domestic flights and the visa are included in every journey, and peak periods carry a supplement that the proposal states. If the shape of the journey is still undecided, begin with the six journeys compared; the calendar follows from it.

Booking early does not mean paying early. A 25% non-refundable deposit secures the booking; the balance is due 60 days before arrival, and any booking made within 60 days of arrival pays in full. The contract exists only once we confirm in writing and the deposit is received, and from that confirmation the price is fixed, except for government action, taxes and fees, or significant currency changes. So deciding a year ahead costs a quarter of the journey, not all of it. The enquiry itself is free and without obligation, and a named journey designer replies within 24 hours.

What sells out first: boats, suites and dated permissions

Three things run out ahead of everything else: whole dahabiyas, suites at the Nile-side hotels, and permissions tied to specific dates. Domestic flights tighten later; most site tickets barely tighten at all. The festive fortnight has a post of its own, Christmas and New Year in Egypt, with its crowd patterns hour by hour and its full booking calendar; the order of loss below holds for every peak week of the year.

Dahabiyas, chartered whole

There are only so many good boats on the Nile, and each sails for one party at a time. Festive dates are claimed nine to twelve months ahead, often for the following year before the current one has finished, and the Easter and Sun Festival weeks follow close behind. A cabin on a large cruise ship is a different commodity: cabins are released with the season's schedules and can usually be booked later. If the river is the heart of your journey, the boat is the first thing to secure and the last thing to trade away.

Suites and Nile-view rooms

At the historic hotels of Luxor and Aswan, suites sell first, then Nile-view rooms, then the rest, in the same order in every busy week. In Cairo the pressure is gentler outside the festive fortnight itself. Hotels are independent suppliers we choose between rather than own, and the right room is the one chosen for your dates; rooms can be swapped to suit while the journey is being designed, but not once the busy week has filled them. Some of Egypt's best-known Nile hotels are also under restoration at present, which narrows the choice further: the Winter Palace in Luxor is closed and due to reopen in July 2027, and the Old Cataract in Aswan has its Nile Wing in renovation until then. Your Luxor hotel is named in the proposal.

Dated permissions

The Empty Plateau, two hours with the Giza plateau opened for your party alone at dawn or before sunset, depends on official permission, and permission is dated: a permission for 28 December is not a permission for the 29th. Nothing is promised. The permission and its cost are requested on booking and confirmed in writing before the balance is due; if it is declined you hear from us and the journey is reshaped. The special tomb tickets in the Valley of the Kings, such as the Tomb of Seti I (KV17), are a different matter: they are bought at the Valley's Visitor Centre on the day, subject to which tombs are open.

What never sells out

Egyptologists are not a bottleneck: yours travels with you from the first day to the last and is arranged with your journey. Most standard site tickets are bought on the day; the exceptions are the Grand Egyptian Museum, sold online only, and the limited Great Pyramid interior tickets, which we book in advance. And the sites themselves never run out: the Valley of the Kings opens at 06:00, and the first hour belongs to whoever arranged to be there, no reservation required. In Egypt, the right hour is a booking decision; the ticket is not.

Booking around events: Easter, the Sun Festival and the 2027 eclipse

Event dates ignore the season around them: treat each one like peak, whatever the month. Egypt's calendar holds three that matter to a private journey: the two Easters, the Abu Simbel Sun Festival, and the total solar eclipse of 2 August 2027.

Easter: two holidays, one spring

Egypt keeps two Easters, and in 2027 they fall five weeks apart: Western Easter on 28 March and Orthodox Easter on 2 May, with Sham Ennessim, the spring outing Egyptians of every background take in the open air, on its Monday, 3 May. Each Easter pulls its own wave of travelling families on school holidays, and the boats and suites around both weeks go six to nine months ahead. The weeks between the two remain calm, which makes late April one of the quieter windows of the spring. Easter moves every year, so fix the dates before fixing anything else.

The Abu Simbel Sun Festival: 22 February and 22 October

Twice a year the rising sun sends its light about 60 metres into the sanctuary, for some 20 to 25 minutes, of the great temple at Abu Simbel and lights three of the four statues there (Ramesses II, Amun-Ra and Ra-Horakhty), leaving Ptah, the Memphite creator god also linked with the underworld, in shadow. The dates are 22 February and 22 October, a Monday and a Friday in 2027, and the February date falls during Ramadan, expected from 8 February, subject to moon sighting. Both dates draw large crowds, demand for the few hotels near the temple rises sharply, and early starts and heavier security are the rule. Treat both dates as peak and book as soon as you know. The calmer way to attend is to overnight at Abu Simbel and walk to the temple before dawn, rather than arrive in the dark with the day-trippers, though neither date should be expected to be quiet.

The total solar eclipse: 2 August 2027

On 2 August 2027 a total solar eclipse crosses Upper Egypt, with totality at Luxor lasting about six minutes and twenty seconds, the longest on easily accessible land this century. A summer date that behaves like Christmas: Luxor's rooms will be claimed far earlier than the season normally demands. We have designed a journey around it, the 2027 eclipse on a private dahabiya, with availability secured, and the date is now under nine months away, so the counsel is simple: if it matters to you, enquire now.

What can wait

More than you might think, and knowing what can wait keeps the booking calm. Site tickets, most Cairo rooms, restaurants and the small river pleasures are decisions for the journey itself, not for the year before.

  • Most standard site tickets. Bought on the day. Which royal tombs are open changes with conservation rotations, so your Egyptologist chooses then, not at booking.
  • Cairo hotels outside the festive fortnight. Weeks, not months, except when a holiday week fills the city.
  • The day-by-day itself. A private proposal is refined together, with hotels swapped to suit and hours moved, right up to travel. Booking early fixes the boat, the rooms and the rate, not every hour of every day.
  • The small pleasures. A table in Cairo, an hour on the river with lunch, tea above the Nile in Aswan: arranged days ahead, sometimes the same day.

Two things genuinely cannot wait. Inside 60 days of arrival, payment is due in full at booking, because the deposit-and-balance rhythm no longer applies. And cancellation terms sharpen as travel approaches: with 60 or more days' notice you lose the deposit only; from 59 to 30 days, half the price; from 29 to 15, three-quarters; at 14 days or fewer, the whole. Travel insurance, separately, is a condition of booking.

And the counsel we give most often: if you are reading this close to a peak week with nothing yet secured, the finer move is not to fight for what remains but to move the date. Mid-January, after Coptic Christmas, or early December, before the fortnight begins, gives you the same weather on a calmer river; our guide to when to go to Egypt compares the whole year. We will say that plainly rather than accept dates we cannot deliver well; the habit has its own post in why we'll sometimes talk you out of a trip.

FAQ

How far in advance should I book a luxury trip to Egypt? Nine to twelve months for Christmas, New Year and event dates such as the Sun Festival; for the 2027 eclipse, now under nine months away, enquire now; six to nine months for Easter; four to six for high winter; three to six for the shoulders; six to ten weeks in summer. The scarcest things, whole dahabiyas and Nile-view suites, are claimed by season, not by month of searching, so the week you choose sets the deadline before anything else does.

How far in advance should I book a Nile cruise? A cabin on a large ship can usually wait until three to six months out, once the season's schedules are on sale. A private dahabiya cannot: the boat is chartered for your party, and peak-week boats are spoken for nine to twelve months ahead. If the river matters most, secure the boat first and let everything else arrange itself around it.

What if I'm already close to a peak week: is it too late? Not necessarily, but the choices narrow. Big-ship cabins and Cairo hotel rooms often remain; whole dahabiyas for the peak nights mostly do not. Shifting a week (mid-January, after Coptic Christmas, or early December before the fortnight begins) restores the choice with the weather intact. Tell us honestly where you are, and we will say what is realistic.

When should I book around the Abu Simbel Sun Festival? As soon as you know your dates. Treat 22 February and 22 October like peak season, because Abu Simbel is a small town and both dates fill its few hotels. Overnighting there, rather than arriving in the dark with the day-trippers, is the calmer way to be at the temple at dawn.

Do I have to pay in full when I book? No. A 25% non-refundable deposit secures the booking; the balance is due 60 days before arrival. Bookings made within 60 days of arrival pay in full, and comprehensive travel insurance is a condition of booking.

Can I arrange a private Egypt journey at short notice? Yes, outside the peaks. Summer journeys come together in six to ten weeks, and short journeys to Cairo alone can move faster still. What short notice costs is choice: the best boats, suites and permissions go first. Tell us the dates and we will say plainly what is still worth taking.

Is Easter as busy as Christmas in Egypt? Nearly, in the holiday weeks. Two Easters pull two waves of travelling families (in 2027, 28 March and 2 May), and Sham Ennessim fills the riverbanks on the Monday after Orthodox Easter. The weeks between the two stay calm, which makes late April one of the better-kept windows of spring.

The takeaway

Book nine to twelve months out for Christmas, New Year and the event dates; six to nine for Easter; four to six for high winter and three to six for the shoulders; weeks, not months, for summer. Let the deposit, not the full price, hold your place. Everything else, from tomb tickets to the hour you face the pyramids, can wait for the journey itself. The next step is a sentence: plan your journey, or message us on WhatsApp, and a named journey designer will reply within 24 hours.
